To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteomic profiling of rCHO cells in a serum-free culture medium supplemented with protein hydrolysates showed the role of energy-metabolism related proteins and importance in prevention of oxidative stress.

the addition of designed mixture of four protein hydrolysates in a chemically defined medium can increase protein productivity of CHO cells by up-regulation of energy metabolism and antioxidant pathways, and down-regulation of apoptosis and stress response pathways.

the addition of hydrolysates in SFM resulted in the upregulation of proteins involved in energy metabolism, antioxidant activity and prevention of oxidative stress, and consequently, increased the productivity of rCHO cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective strategy for the optimization of protein expression in rCHO cells.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are differentially expressed during the cultivation of CHO cells in a chemically defined medium supplemented with protein hydrolysates.
the proteomic profiling of rCHO cells grown in the designed media and provides valuable information for the improvement of rCHO cells in the biopharmaceutical industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

protein hydrolysates have a significant role in the regulation of cellular metabolic pathways and protein expression in rCHO cells cultivated under the condition of protein hydrolysate addition to the media.
protein expression can be enhanced by a combination of protein hydrolysate additives and a chemically defined medium.
protein hydrolysates are not just a supplement for media, but also a tool for engineering rCHO cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein expression is enhanced by a designed mixture of hydrolysate additives, and the proteomic analysis revealed that metabolic pathways, energy production and oxidative stress were involved in this enhancement.
the designed mixture of four hydrolysates could be a promising additive for enhancing protein production in CHO cell cultures.
the addition of hydrolysates to the SFM resulted in the up-regulation of the proteins involved in the energy metabolism, antioxidant activity and the cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteomics can be used to understand the molecular mechanisms of media composition optimization.
proteomic analysis can be used to identify the mechanisms of protein overexpression in CHO cells.
proteomics can provide new insights into biochemical pathways for a media composition optimization.
